items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 26 at 9:53PM AKDT until October 27 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 7
inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph. Visibility could be
reduced to less than a half mile at times.

* WHERE...Dalton Highway Summits, Fortymile Country, Upper Chena
River Valley, White Mountains, and High Terrain South of the Yukon
River.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could reduce visibility below one half
mile at times.
items.areas: Dalton Highway Summits; White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River; Fortymile Country; Upper Chena River Valley
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 26 at 9:53PM AKDT until October 27 at 8:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...North winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph expected.

* WHERE...Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...From 9 AM to 8 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make travel difficult. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 26 at 5:02PM AKDT until October 28 at 12:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast

* WHEN...From 10 PM Tuesday to 10 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Southeast winds will become strong and gusty
by Tuesday night. Winds are expected to be strongest along the
coast. Winds will begin to diminish Wednesday morning.
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 26 at 1:38PM AKDT until October 28 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 1 to 3 feet above the normal high
tide line at Stebbins, St. Michael, Unalakleet, Koyuk and
Shaktoolik, and 3 to 5 feet above the normal high tide line at
Elim. Water levels are expected to peak Tuesday evening.

* WHERE...Eastern Norton Sound Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Wind gusts will peak around 40 to 50 mph
out of the south/southeast.
items.areas: Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 26 at 10:59AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend. 1-3 more inches of precipitation
are expected by the end of the week which will keep water levels
high.
